title: Everyone was sharing stuff made with GPT 6 Astra, so I had to give it a try.
author: Taniai_
selftext:
Hey everyone,

As you’ve probably seen lately, people have been sharing crazy game videos and software projects made with GPT 6 Astra all over X, Instagram, and Reddit. So yesterday, I wanted to give it a try with Godot (which I had zero experience with) just to understand and see its limits. It took around 3 hours and ate through 45% of my Pro plan’s weekly limit.

I should mention that I have no commercial goals or expectations with this. I even thought it might give some of the developers here an idea for a game. The idea actually came from a study, and I think it’s something we’ve all wondered about at least once.

The premise is simple: **Most men think they could land a passenger plane with outside help and guidance.** As a pilot myself, knowing what’s actually involved, I tried to make a game with GPT Astra that would offer a simulation experience with controls as close to reality as possible. If you’re curious about the result, or whether you could actually land that plane, you can try it at the link below.

👇🏻👇🏻👇🏻👇🏻

[https://landifyoucan.com](https://landifyoucan.com)

I can barely bring myself to call it a game, but this thing that came out of the experiment might give us all an idea of how the industry is changing and what’s coming over the next few years.

For anyone curious, it chose Godot 4 as the engine and created the models itself in Blender using real-world references. It put everything together through a chain of around 30 prompts, with my feedback mostly focused on the mechanics, how the sea looked, the skybox, and finally, replaying the crash or successful landing once it was over.

comments.author: sevenoutdb
comments.body:
Pretty thrilling actually. Well done. This kind of crisis simulator seems like fertile ground. I would love a little bit more info about what good looks like, e.g. what angle (pitch?) should the plane be at when the wheels touch down, and at what speed.  I played it a few times, first try, 2 survived, 1 injured, 45 landing gear dmg, 40 air frame, second time, 0 injured, 40% landing gear, 35% air frame damage. 

nice work!
